verification_report.summary:
The entire submitted proof is correct for every hypothetical smooth solution under the stated hypotheses and accepted linear inputs. The sequential audit found no critical errors or gaps. Detailed deductions and reference comparisons are preserved in memory/stw_czero_01/statement_checks.jsonl and reference_checks.jsonl.

At extrema the first-order correction vanishes, and wedging the signed complex Hessian with gamma^(n-2) gives the stated order of Gamma_u. Determinant monotonicity and det(cofactor H)=(det H)^(n-1) give exactly the displayed bounds for b. This uses volume monotonicity, without assuming that the positive (1,1)-root map preserves matrix order.

The fixed operator L is real, smooth, uniformly elliptic, has only second- and first-order terms, and satisfies Lu>=-C0. The manuscript's positive-adjoint argument applies to drift: the maximum principle gives a constant kernel, elliptic homotopy gives index zero, and Fredholm plus the strong minimum principle gives a fixed smooth strictly positive adjoint probability nu. Inverting L on functions of zero nu-mean gives the displayed Green representation with the correct minus sign. For real dimension 2n>=4, the kernel after that minus sign has a positive leading singularity of order distance^(2-2n). Standard uniform local Green estimates and compactness bound its negative part and its integrals. Adding one constant makes K nonnegative and preserves the representation because integral Lv dnu=0. Neither symmetry nor a zero-mean condition on the shifted K is required. Evaluation at a maximum gives integral(-u)dnu<=C; the fixed positive density transfers this to any fixed smooth volume.

A finite collection of nested holomorphic charts provides a common radius and uniform coefficient, inverse-metric and volume bounds after translation and rescaling at any minimum. Every slope with norm below epsilon/2 has an interior supporting minimum for v=u+epsilon|x|^2, which lies in A. The set A is measurable and actually compact inside the ball: u>=M and v<=M+epsilon/2 imply |x|<=1/sqrt(2). Its gradient image contains the slope ball. The smooth area formula, including multiplicity, proves the displayed area inequality; injectivity, a measurable selection of contacts and global convexity are unnecessary.

On A, |Du|<=5epsilon/2 and D2u>=-2epsilon I. The complex Hessian lower bound, positivity of wedging with gamma^(n-2), and the small first-order correction give Q_u>=cI after choosing epsilon from fixed data. The equation gives det Q_u<=D through exp((n-1)(F+b)). Hence every eigenvalue is at most D/c^(n-1). Contracting Gamma_u with gamma and subtracting the background and bounded first-order term bounds the gamma trace of the complex Hessian of u. Adding epsilon|x|^2 gives a nonnegative complex Hessian for v, so metric comparison bounds its Euclidean trace. The real trace is four times the complex trace. Arithmetic-geometric mean then uniformly bounds det D2v on A. No nonlinear uniform ellipticity away from A is used.

The area inequality consequently gives |A|>=c2>0. Uniform volume comparison gives integral_A(-u)dx<=C3, while -u>=max(0,-M-epsilon/2) on A. Thus the last displayed inequality remains valid even when -M-epsilon/2 is negative, and -M<=epsilon/2+C3/c2. Together with the scalar bound and sup u=0, this proves the requested estimate.

The saved source and [the original arXiv v3 paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.02762v3) confirm Propositions 10-11 and Remark 12, pp. 8-11. Required theorem searches were followed by web fallback to verify the original attribution. Proposition 10 assumes a C-subsolution; the submitted proof reconstructs the needed argument directly. Proposition 11 uses global supporting contacts, whereas the submitted larger set A is justified independently. Remark 12 explicitly treats first-order gradient terms. The exact translation is alpha=gamma, source potential phi=u/(2pi), chi=star_gamma(gamma0^(n-1))/(n-1)!, and source logarithmic density h=(n-1)(F+b). Thus the ansatz, factorials and determinant exponent agree.

All dependencies are: smooth finite-dimensional calculus and compactness; finite holomorphic charts and fixed metric/volume comparisons; positive (n-1,n-1) roots, cofactor/determinant algebra, positivity of wedge products, elementary Hodge-star identities for the reference translation, Hessian trace identities and arithmetic-geometric mean; standard smooth real linear elliptic maximum/minimum principles, regularity, Fredholm alternative, index invariance and Green kernel estimates; and the smooth area formula. The standing conventions and prior adjoint proof were checked in conventions.tex, chapter_gauduchon.tex, chapter_smooth_equations.tex (the current location of the requested chapter_equations.tex material), and section_gauduchon_volume_adjoint.tex. The Gauduchon identity is harmlessly redundant for this particular estimate. All constants depend only on fixed geometry and ||F||_infty. STW existence or estimates, nonlinear ABP/C0 theorems, derivatives of F, BMP and PVP are not dependencies. The concluding limitation to a zeroth-order estimate is accurate. The book was not edited.
